chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Mu'alla, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever a drinker of wine was brought to him, would whip him. Then if he was brought to him a second time, he would whip him. Then if he was brought to him a third time, he would strike his neck.
ai.seo_question: What is the progressive punishment for wine drinkers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific judicial practice of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) regarding the consumption of wine, establishing a clear progression from corporal punishment to capital punishment. While later jurists debated whether this execution was a specific ruling for the Prophet or a general rule for the community, this hadith serves as a primary evidence for the severity of khamr in early Islamic jurisprudence. It underscores the transition from the initial gradual prohibition to the final, strict enforcement of the penalty for habitual consumption.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Moala, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever they came with a drinker of the wine, would whip him. Then if they came with him for a second time, he<sup>saww</sup> would whip him. They if they came up with him for a third time, he<sup>saww</sup> would strike his neck’.
